title: Token load scenarios and GPU mix heatmap Q3 2026
summary: A candidate provisioning matrix for Q3 2026 that translates regional GPU fleet sizes into tokens/sec capacity and QPS headroom under three peak scenarios (likely, aggressive, stress). Includes a recommended target that builds in operational headroom and a short action list for procurement and autoscale config changes.
assumptions: baseline tokens/sec per full-GPU (effective across model mix) = 900 tps. average tokens per request = 240. baseline util = current observed avg in-region (see matrix). target provisioning util = 70% for steady-state SLA. headroom target = 20% above required GPUs for the likely-peak scenario. network/KV caching effects baked into effective tps; streaming-request mix will reduce QPS but increase token tail — accounted for by conservative tokens/request estimate. margin for model upgrades (L->M shift) considered in sensitivity analysis.

Notes: Effective tps/GPU is a blended value across models we currently serve. Required GPUs computed as ceil(peak_tps / (effective_tps/GPU * provisioning_util)), provisioning_util=0.70. QPS = peak_tps / avg_tokens_per_request (240).
totals: Total current capacity (tps) = 219600. Total likely peak tps = 357300. Total target GPUs (post-headroom) = 684. Current total GPUs = 400. Total additional GPUs required to hit target = 284. Total likely peak QPS = 1489. Interpretation: with current fleet and baseline utilization we do not meet likely peak without adding ~284 GPUs or shifting routing/quantization to increase effective tps/GPU.
sensitivity_analysis: 1) If effective tps/GPU improves by 15% (software/kernels/quantization), tokens/GPU -> 1035: target GPUs drop from 684 -> ~596 (saving ~88 GPUs). 2) If avg tokens/request increases to 320 (longer responses), QPS at likely peak drops to 1116 and the tail pressure increases — this requires either more GPUs or stricter per-request token caps. 3) If target provisioning util increased to 75% (riskier for latency spikes), required GPUs decrease by ~7%. 4) Regional burst risk: us-west-2 and us-east-1 account for ~66% of total peak tps; prioritize procurement and quick-burst capacity in those regions.
operational_notes: - Autoscale knobs: reduce cool-down for burst pools to 60s, pre-warm ramp for announced marketing events, enable cross-region failover policy to degrade to cheaper model variants at 60% sustained overload. - Observability: add a dashboard tile that shows tokens/sec headroom per region and GPUs available for warm-up. - Billing: flagged for review with finance for reserve-contract sizing; dedicated pool pricing likely required for capacity commit in us-east and us-west.
scaling_playbook: 1) Immediate (0-30 days): request procurement approval for +80 GPUs targeted to us-east-1 and us-west-2 (split 50/30), add templates for rapid cloud quota increases. 2) Short term (30-90 days): reorder capacity to reach +200 GPUs across key regions, implement autoscale pre-warming and shorten scale-out path. 3) Medium term (90-180 days): negotiate reserved capacity for baseline and burst credits, review model quantization rollout to improve tps/GPU. 4) Long term (>180 days): diversify GPU types (add efficient M-class hardware), invest in compilation/kernel work to raise effective tps by 15-25%.

Please check region-level traffic forecasts (product telemetry) and surface any upcoming marketing or partner events that could change multipliers. If you adjust the effective tps/GPU assumption, update the CSV here and re-run the totals block.
